name: XML Tagging / Schema Specs
executive_summary: Explicit structural delimiters (XML tags, markdown fences, schema specs) to separate instructions, context, and output zones. Reduces parsing errors, improves model comprehension, and mitigates injection risk.
description: XML tagging and schema specifications provide unambiguous boundaries between different semantic zones in a prompt. By wrapping instructions in <instructions>, context in <context>, and expected output in <output_format>, the model can better distinguish trusted instructions from untrusted user input.
when_to_use: Any production prompt where instructions and user input coexist.
When parsing errors occur due to ambiguous boundaries.
As a defense-in-depth measure against prompt injection.
when_not_to_use: Simple conversational prompts with no structured sections.
When the model is known to struggle with XML formatting.
When token minimization is critical and tags add unacceptable overhead.
known_pitfalls: Malformed XML (unclosed tags) can confuse the model.
Over-nesting tags adds token overhead without proportional benefit.
Not all models handle XML equally well; test with your target model.

primary_source.title: Prompt Engineering Best Practices: XML Tagging
